what_happened: The absorbed obsidian-memory sub-task's existing declaration (settings-fragment.json: npx -y @anthropic-ai/obsidian-claude-code-mcp@latest) names a non-existent npm package -- confirmed via a direct npm registry API query (registry.npmjs.org returns 404/Not found). The real project (iansinnott/obsidian-claude-code-mcp) is an Obsidian PLUGIN that Claude Code discovers through its native /ide integration (lock files under ~/.claude/ide/), not a command Claude Code spawns via .mcp.json or npx at all. OBSIDIAN_WS_PORT as an env var name also does not appear in that project's documentation.

A prior, already-completed task (reconcile_mcp_registration_surfaces) left agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/mcp-server-ownership.md already documenting the registration/permission split, the workspace-trust gate, and the session-start snapshot trap in detail -- most of the factual groundwork the dispatch asked for already existed and only needed locating, not re-deriving.

agent-system/extensions/core/docs/architecture/extension-system.md line ~227 still states only ~/.claude.json registers MCP servers, omitting .mcp.json, which contradicts the newer mcp-server-ownership.md. The same doc's merge.lua function table also lists merge_opencode_agents()/unmerge_opencode_agents(), which no longer exist in lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/merge.lua (opencode.json is now a fully computed artifact). Separately, lua/neotex/plugins/ai/claude/extensions/manifest_spec.lua and the shared/ copy both carry a test 'should reject manifest with invalid merge_targets type' that the current generic validate_merge_targets() (no closed type-name set) does not actually enforce.

Plan-authoring verification run of lua/neotex/plugins/ai/claude/extensions/manifest_spec.lua found a pre-existing RED test ('should reject manifest with invalid merge_targets type', 16 Success / 1 Fail): it asserts a closed-set merge_targets validator the generic implementation never had, and it directly contradicts the new mcp key validating. Folded into the plan as Phase 2 with a recorded design decision (keep the validator open-set, repair the test to assert the real contract) rather than silently widening the validator.

Two dispatch-supplied inputs removed most planning uncertainty up front: the Prior Decisions block settled the obsidian-memory half (Option 1, drop the npx wiring) so no user_decision needed re-raising, and the research report's end-to-end read of the merge-target dispatch path meant the only codebase work left at plan time was confirming exact anchors. Also found an exact structural precedent for the verification harness (test-deploy-orphans.sh drives the engine headlessly against a scratch tree), which turned a speculative fixture phase into a modelled one.
